title: Kolkata civic polls slip as election body defers final voter rolls for KMC and six others
dek: The State Election Commission has put off the 12 November publication of final rolls for Kolkata, Howrah and five municipalities, with no new date. An official said polls could not now be held before 30 November.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
West Bengal's State Election Commission (SEC) on Thursday postponed publication of the final voter rolls for the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) and six other civic bodies, which had been due on 12 November, making it unlikely that Kolkata will have an elected board by early December as the government had planned.

The SEC did not announce a new date. In a letter to the KMC's district municipal election officer and to the district magistrates of South 24 Parganas, Howrah, Jalpaiguri, Kalimpong and Purba Medinipur, SEC secretary Arindam Mani said the date "is hereby extended" and that the revised date "will be notified in due course", The Times of India reported.

## Which civic bodies are affected

The deferment covers the bodies expected to vote in the first phase: the KMC, the Howrah Municipal Corporation, and the municipalities of Bally, Haldia, Dhupguri, Kalimpong and Kurseong.

## Why the date moved

An SEC official told The Times of India that under the rules the final roll must be published on the seventh day after the notification announcing the elections. Because the poll notification was not issued on Thursday, 5 November, the roll date had to be pushed back. "Under the circumstances, elections cannot be held before Nov 30," the official said.

The notification itself is on hold because of a court case. On 28 October a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court reserved its order on an appeal against the redrawing of Kolkata's wards from 144 to 209, and recorded that no notification calling KMC elections would be issued until 6 November, when it was expected to rule, LiveLaw reported. The petitioner argues that the KMC's Administrator had no power to redraw the wards and that the exercise amounted to gerrymandering. The state says the Administrator holds all the corporation's powers and that delimitation can be challenged only through an election petition after the polls.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had said the KMC would have a new board before the first week of December. The corporation's elected board was dissolved on 8 June and the city has since been run by an Administrator.

## What the parties say

Opposition parties have said there are errors in the delimitation and booth maps and want the elections held only after the Election Commission of India publishes its revised rolls in January. "The voter list is erroneous, with names of several dead voters still on it," Ashutosh Chatterjee of the Congress told The Times of India. The Bengal Congress has also written to the poll authorities about what it calls discrepancies in the KMC's delimitation and booth maps, The Hindu reported.

CPI(M) leader Kallol Majumdar alleged that the BJP wanted to delay the polls because of internal disputes over candidates. BJP leader Sisir Bajoria rejected that. "We want elections on time. But the opposition wants to defer it as the parties are not prepared," he said. Ratna Sur, a Trinamool district chairperson in south Kolkata, said election officials were "unprepared and clueless".

## What happens next

The High Court's ruling on the ward delimitation is expected on Friday, 6 November. If the court allows the state to go ahead, the SEC can issue the poll notification and set a new date for the final rolls; the elections would then follow at least a week later.
